analysis.investment_thesis: Eureka Forbes trades at INR 482 against a calculated Graham Number of ~INR 211, a 128% premium to intrinsic value by my formula — Mr. Market is paying a steep price for a brand with a 3.71% ROE. At P/E of 47x and P/B of 2.07x, there is no margin of safety whatsoever for the disciplined investor.
key_strengths: Near-zero debt (D/E: 0.02) and growing OCF (INR 246 Cr in FY25) — balance sheet I can respect
Free cash flow consistently positive and growing: INR 167→169→190 Cr over three years
59% gross margin suggests a services/consumables model with real pricing power
key_risks: P/E of 47.3x — more than three times my ceiling of 15x — bakes in a decade of flawless execution
ROE of 3.71% and ROCE of 5.07% are below India's risk-free rate; management is destroying real value per rupee of equity
Meaningful earnings history spans only FY2023–2025; pre-2022 figures reflect a restructuring stub, not a going concern — Graham demands 5+ years of proven earnings
red_flags: Graham Number ~INR 211 vs. market price INR 482 — stock must fall 56% just to reach fair value by my formula
Operating margin of only 7.97% leaves little buffer against any demand or cost shock
Capex jumped from INR 28 Cr to INR 60 Cr in FY25 while ROE remains depressed — capital allocation efficiency is questionable
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Eureka Forbes fails my core quantitative filters on nearly every dimension. The P/E of 47.3x is 3x my absolute ceiling; the P/B of 2.07x exceeds my 1.5x threshold; and my Graham Number — √(22.5 × EPS ~₹8.5 × BVPS ~₹234) — yields approximately ₹211, less than half the current price of ₹482. Mr. Market is charging a speculative premium for a company whose ROE is 3.71% — a figure that barely compensates for inflation, let alone the cost of equity. I have no interest in businesses where shareholders earn less than they could in a fixed deposit.

The balance sheet, I will concede, is clean: debt of just ₹91 Cr against equity of ₹4,520 Cr is commendable, and the interest coverage of ~44x is impeccable. Free cash flow is real and growing. But virtue in the balance sheet does not excuse an extravagant price. The company's verifiable earnings history is only three years deep (FY23–FY25), as the pre-2022 revenue of ₹8 Cr reflects a corporate restructuring shell, not a business. I require five or more years of uninterrupted profits before I trust a number, and here I have three. At half the current price — around ₹210–240 — this might be worth a second look. At ₹482, the intelligent investor must firmly decline.
